items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And he played with Bird and Diz and Miles and all those people.

ctx.x: Yeah. [inaudible] I think it was my first big record date with Allen Eager. Allen Eager — you know who Teddy “Fats” Reig was? Teddy Reig was the first guy to ever record Bird and Diz, for Savoy Records. He ran that company. And Teddy weighed about 400 pounds. And Allen Eager was the hot white tenor player. He was like the first guy that played like Prez, not that well known. But he had be — he played bebop but like Prez. And he played with Bird and Diz and Miles and all those people. Well Allen loved me and Allen…

Allen said, “You want to play ‘Jordu’?” and I said, “play the melody and I’ll learn” you know. It was really fast. He played it and I played it right after him. And so you know we always played short choruses, maybe 16 bars, because records in those days were three minutes. So but I didn’t know the release chord changes. So I walked over to Duke, who was out in the boonies mentally at the time, he was stoned out, and I said to him, I whispered in his ear, I said, “Duke, what’s the changes in the release?” He…
